site.name: Maid of Erin Mine
overview: The Maid of Erin was one of the named mines in Leadville’s dense Carbonate Hill mining landscape. Its history overlaps with neighboring properties but the mine remains a distinct Remnant site.
The property is useful for understanding how Leadville’s mines changed through operating, leasing, dump-processing, and later environmental-remediation periods.

timeline.text: The Maid of Erin operated as part of the heavily developed Carbonate Hill district.
Historical property records document leasing and later processing of mine-dump material.
EPA historic-property documentation records consolidation and remediation of waste associated with Maid of Erin, Wolftone, and Mahala areas.
The site is interpreted as a distinct mine component within a tightly packed historic and remediated mining landscape.

moreHistory: EPA California Gulch documentation provides unusually useful information because it preserves both operating history and later changes to the physical mining landscape.
Maid of Erin should not be merged with Wolftone or other nearby Carbonate Hill properties simply because their histories and remediation areas overlap.
USGS Leadville district studies provide the larger geologic and ore-deposit framework needed to understand why so many mines were concentrated in this area.
